prerequisites: Mathematics: Calculus II and Differential Equations (V12G340V01204)
It is necessary to have passed or be enrolled in all subjects from courses lower than the one in which this subject is placed.
It is recommended that the student has passed Physics II from the 1st year or has equivalent knowledge of Thermodynamic Principles.

syllabus_topics: Review of the First and Second Principles of Thermodynamics
Properties of Pure Substances: Use of Tables and Diagrams
Analysis of Open Systems According to the First and Second Laws of Thermodynamics
Applications of Thermodynamic Engineering: Power Cycles and Refrigeration Cycles
Fundamental Concepts and Principles of Heat Transfer
Heat Transfer by Conduction. Unidirectional Steady-State Conduction
Heat Transfer by Convection: Fundamentals and Convection Correlations
Heat Transfer by Radiation: General Principles. Thermal Radiation
assessment_rules: The course can be passed through two modalities: Continuous Assessment or Global Assessment. In Continuous Assessment, the final grade is determined by summing points from various continuous assessment activities. For Global Assessment, which covers all course content and accounts for 100% of the maximum grade, students must officially renounce continuous assessment; it consists of a written problem-solving test (70-80% of the final grade) and a specific test with theoretical questions and/or an objective question test (20-30% of the final grade). A final grade of 5 points or higher is required to pass the course in either the ordinary or extraordinary evaluation opportunity. Unethical behavior (copying, plagiarism, unauthorized electronic devices) will result in a failing grade of 0.0 for the entire academic year.
